# Dockerfile – Hermes Agent (Debian Bookworm)
# =============================================================================
# Hermes Agent: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com
# Build: docker build -t hermes-agent:latest .
# =============================================================================
ARG DEBIAN_VERSION=bookworm

FROM debian:${DEBIAN_VERSION}-slim AS build

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. System dependencies for the install script
# ------------------------------------------------------------
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update -qq; \
    apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates \
        curl \
        git \
        ; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Install Hermes Agent (non-interactive)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Installs system-wide so the hermes binary is in PATH for any user.
# --non-interactive skips terminal-interactive stages.
ARG HERMES_BRANCH=main
ARG HERMES_COMMIT=""

RUN set -eux; \
    INSTALL_ARGS=""; \
    if [ -n "${HERMES_COMMIT}" ]; then \
      INSTALL_ARGS="${INSTALL_ARGS} --commit ${HERMES_COMMIT}"; \
    fi; \
    curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh \
      | bash -s -- \
        --non-interactive \
        --branch "${HERMES_BRANCH}" \
        --dir /opt/hermes-agent \
        ${INSTALL_ARGS} \
        ; \
    /opt/hermes-agent/bin/hermes --version

# =============================================================================
# Runtime stage — smaller final image, no build-time dependencies
# =============================================================================
FROM debian:${DEBIAN_VERSION}-slim

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Runtime system dependencies
# ------------------------------------------------------------
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update -qq; \
    apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates \
        git \
        ; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Copy Hermes from build stage
# ------------------------------------------------------------
COPY --from=build /opt/hermes-agent /opt/hermes-agent
RUN ln -s /opt/hermes-agent/bin/hermes /usr/local/bin/hermes

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create non-root user
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# UID/GID can be overridden at build time to match the host user.
ARG USER_ID=1000
ARG GROUP_ID=1000

RUN set -eux; \
    groupadd --gid "${GROUP_ID}" --non-unique hermes; \
    useradd  --uid "${USER_ID}" --gid "${GROUP_ID}" \
             --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin \
             hermes; \
    install -d -o hermes -g hermes -m 0755 \
        /config \
        /data/rw \
        /vault \
        /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Volumes & environment
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Persistent Hermes configuration (mount or named volume).
VOLUME /config

# Optional Obsidian vault mount for Hermes to read/write freely.
VOLUME /vault

# Read-only input data from host.
VOLUME /data/ro

# Read-write working data from host.
VOLUME /data/rw

ENV HERMES_HOME=/config
ENV HERMES_PORT=8080

EXPOSE ${HERMES_PORT}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Entrypoint
# ------------------------------------------------------------
WORKDIR /data/rw
USER hermes

COPY --chown=hermes:hermes docker-entrypoint.sh /docker-entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod 755 /docker-entrypoint.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/docker-entrypoint.sh"]
CMD ["serve"]", "path": "/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker/Dockerfile"}

{"content": "#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# docker-entrypoint.sh – Hermes Agent Container Entrypoint
# =============================================================================
# Responsibilities:
#   1. Ensure config.yaml exists (or create a minimal working one)
#   2. Ensure the .env secrets file exists or warn
#   3. Optionally detect a mounted Obsidian vault at /vault
#   4. Start hermes in serve mode
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

HERMES_HOME="${HERMES_HOME:-/config}"
HERMES_PORT="${HERMES_PORT:-8080}"
CONFIG_FILE="${HERMES_HOME}/config.yaml"
ENV_FILE="${HERMES_HOME}/.env"

# -----------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: create a minimal config.yaml
# -----------------------------------------------------------
create_minimal_config() {
    echo "==> No Hermes configuration found. Creating minimal config.yaml ..."

    cat > "${CONFIG_FILE}" <<- 'CONFEOF'
# Minimal Hermes configuration — generated by docker-entrypoint.sh
# Replace with your own config.yaml mounted at /config/config.yaml
#
# Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration

# --- Model provider (required for chat, optional for serve mode) ---
# Set via `hermes config set` or editing this file.
# Uncomment and set your preferred provider:
#default_model: gpt-4o
#default_provider: openai

# --- Server mode (serve) ---
# These defaults are overridden by CLI flags.
server:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: ${HERMES_PORT}
CONFEOF

    sed -i "s/\${HERMES_PORT}/${HERMES_PORT}/g" "${CONFIG_FILE}"
    echo "==> Created ${CONFIG_FILE}"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: ensure .env exists or warn
# -----------------------------------------------------------
check_env_file() {
    if [ ! -f "${ENV_FILE}" ]; then
        cat > "${ENV_FILE}" <<- 'ENVEOF'
# Hermes secrets — mount your own .env to /config/.env
# API keys for LLM providers. At least one provider must be configured.
# Examples:
# OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
# OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...
ENVEOF
        echo "==> WARNING: ${ENV_FILE} is a stub. Add your API keys before starting Hermes."
    fi
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: detect and report an optional Obsidian vault mount
# -----------------------------------------------------------
check_vault_mount() {
    if [ ! -d /vault ]; then
        return
    fi

    if [ -z "$(ls -A /vault 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        echo "==> /vault is present but empty — no Obsidian vault mounted."
        return
    fi

    if [ -d /vault/.obsidian ]; then
        echo "==> Obsidian vault detected at /vault (full read/write access)"
    else
        echo "==> Directory mounted at /vault (no .obsidian marker found — still usable as a writable data dir)"
    fi
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# -----------------------------------------------------------
cd /data/rw

case "${1:-serve}" in
    serve|server)
        if [ ! -f "${CONFIG_FILE}" ]; then
            create_minimal_config
        else
            echo "==> Using existing config: ${CONFIG_FILE}"
        fi

        check_env_file
        check_vault_mount

        if [ -d /data/rw ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u' /data/rw)" != "$(id -u)" ]; then
            echo "==> Adjusting /data/rw ownership to user $(id -un) ..."
            chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /data/rw 2>/dev/null || true
        fi

        echo "==> Starting Hermes server on 0.0.0.0:${HERMES_PORT} ..."
        exec hermes serve \
            --host 0.0.0.0 \
            --port "${HERMES_PORT}" \
            --skip-build
        ;;

    init|setup)
        echo "==> Interactive Hermes setup mode."
        echo "==> Configure your provider, model, and credentials."
        echo "==> Type 'exit' or Ctrl-D when done."
        echo ""
        exec hermes setup
        ;;

    config)
        shift
        exec hermes config "$@"
        ;;

    shell|bash)
        exec /bin/bash "$@"
        ;;

    *)
        exec hermes "$@"
        ;;
esac", "path": "/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker/docker-entrypoint.sh"}

# docker-compose.yml – Hermes Agent Container
# =============================================================================
# Quick start:
#   1. Create ./hermes-config/config.yaml and ./hermes-config/.env
#      (or run `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` once)
#   2. docker compose up -d
#   3. Connect your Hermes GUI client to http://host:8080
# =============================================================================
services:
  hermes:
    image: hermes-agent:latest
    build:
      context: .
      # Optional: pin a specific Hermes commit
      # args:
      #   HERMES_COMMIT: abc123def
    container_name: hermes
    restart: unless-stopped

    # ---- Port mapping ----
    ports:
      - "${HERMES_PORT:-8080}:${HERMES_PORT:-8080}"

    # ---- Volumes ----
    volumes:
      # Persistent Hermes configuration (config.yaml + .env).
      # Create it once manually or via `docker compose run --rm hermes-init`.
      - ./hermes-config:/config:rw

      # (Optional) Mount an existing Obsidian vault for full read/write access.
      # Uncomment and point to your vault directory:
      # - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw

      # Read-only input data from host.
      - ./input:/data/ro:ro

      # Read-write working data from host.
      - ./workspace:/data/rw:rw

    # ---- Environment ----
    environment:
      - HERMES_PORT=${HERMES_PORT:-8080}
      - HERMES_HOME=/config

    # ---- Security hardening ----
    read_only: false
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    cap_add:
      - CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE

    # ---- Health check ----
    # Hermes serve exposes no HTTP health endpoint; TCP connect is used as
    # a best-effort liveness probe.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT:-8080} 2>/dev/null && exit 0 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ---- One-shot interactive setup service ----
  # Run once to create the config files:
  #   docker compose run --rm hermes-init
  hermes-init:
    image: hermes-agent:latest
    container_name: hermes-init
    profiles:
      - init
    volumes:
      - ./hermes-config:/config:rw
    environment:
      - HERMES_HOME=/config
    entrypoint: ["/docker-entrypoint.sh"]
    command: ["init"]

{"content": "# Hermes Agent -- Docker

Run [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) by **Nous Research**
inside a lean Debian container and connect from an external GUI client.

## Architecture

```
  +--------------------------------------------+
  |  Host                                      |
  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
  |  | ./input/         |-->| /data/ro       | |  Read-only input
  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |
  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
  |  | ./workspace/     |<--| /data/rw       | |  Read-write work data
  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |
  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
  |  | ./hermes-        |-->| /config        | |  Persistent config
  |  | config/          |   | (yaml + .env)  | |
  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
  |  | /path/to/vault   |-->| /vault         | |  Optional Obsidian vault
  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |  (read-write, opt-in)
  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
  |                                            |
  |  GUI client --port 8080--> container      |
  +--------------------------------------------+
```

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Multi-stage build (bookworm-slim) |
| `docker-compose.yml` | Service definition + init service |
| `docker-entrypoint.sh` | Config check, initialisation, server start |
| `.env.example` | Environment variable template (copy to `.env`) |
| `README.md` | This document |

## Build

```bash
docker compose build
```

To pin a specific Hermes version, set `HERMES_COMMIT` in `.env` or pass it
as a build arg:

```bash
docker compose build --build-arg HERMES_COMMIT=abc123def
```

## Quick Start

### 1. Provide Configuration

**Option A -- Pre-made config (recommended for automation):**

Create two files inside `./hermes-config/`:

**`hermes-config/config.yaml`**:
```yaml
server:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8080
```

**`hermes-config/.env`**:
```bash
# At least one LLM provider API key
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...
```

**Option B -- Interactive setup (run once):**

```bash
docker compose run --rm hermes-init
```

The wizard steps you through provider, model, and API key choices. The
generated config is saved to `./hermes-config/` and is picked up by the
regular service afterwards.

### 2. Start

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

### 3. Connect

Point your Hermes GUI client (desktop app) at:

```
http://<host-ip>:8080
```

## Port Configuration

```bash
# Via .env
HERMES_PORT=9090

# Or inline
HERMES_PORT=9090 docker compose up -d
```

## Data Directories

| Host path | Container | Mode | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------|------|---------|
| `./input/` | `/data/ro` | `:ro` | Read-only host input data |
| `./workspace/` | `/data/rw` | `:rw` | Read-write work and results |
| `./hermes-config/` | `/config` | `:rw` | Persistent configuration + secrets |
| *(optional)* `/vault` | `/vault` | `:rw` | Optional Obsidian vault mount |

## Optional Obsidian Vault Mount

You can optionally mount an existing Obsidian vault into the container so
Hermes has read/write access to it -- the same freedom it has with its own
Hermes Vault (HV) in a non-Docker setup.

This is **purely optional**. The container works perfectly without it.

### How It Works

- The vault is mounted at `/vault` inside the container.
- Hermes runs as the `hermes` user and has full r/w access to everything
  under `/vault`.
- The standard Hermes tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `search_files`,
  `patch`) work on `/vault/...` paths without extra configuration.
- Hermes can browse, create, and edit notes, search file contents, and
  manage markdown files -- everything it does with its own HV.

### Setup

Uncomment and adjust the vault volume in `docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
volumes:
  # ... other mounts ...
  - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw
```

Replace the path with your actual vault location, for example:

```yaml
  - /home/user/syncthing/obsidian-vault:/vault:rw
```

### UID/GID Considerations

The container user `hermes` has UID 1000 by default (configurable via build
args `USER_ID`/`GROUP_ID`). Your vault files must be readable and writable
by that UID. The two easiest approaches:

1. **Match the build UID to your host user** (recommended):
   ```bash
   docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
   ```

2. **Make vault files group-accessible**:
   ```bash
   chmod -R g+rws /path/to/your/vault
   ```

### What Hermes Can Do With the Vault

Once mounted, Hermes can perform all vault operations it normally does with
its own HV:

| Operation | How |
|-----------|-----|
| Read notes | `read_file(path="/vault/some-note.md")` |
| Write new notes | `write_file(path="/vault/new-note.md", content="...")` |
| Search contents | `search_files(pattern="...", path="/vault")` |
| Patch existing notes | `patch(path="/vault/some-note.md", old_string="...", new_string="...")` |
| Navigate directories | `terminal(command="ls /vault/")` |
| Create/manage markdown | All standard Hermes tools |

The entrypoint script detects the vault mount on startup and reports
whether an Obsidian vault (`.obsidian/` marker) is present.

## Permission Model (UID/GID)

The Hermes process runs as user `hermes` (UID 1000 / GID 1000 by default).

**If your host user has a different UID:**

1. Check your UID:
   ```bash
   id -u
   ```

2. Rebuild with matching UID:
   ```bash
   docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
   ```

3. Ensure `./workspace/` is writable on the host:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p workspace input hermes-config
   chmod 755 workspace
   ```

4. Or fix permissions after the first start:
   ```bash
   chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) workspace
   ```

## Initialisation Strategy

### The Problem

`hermes setup` is an interactive wizard. In a headless container it must
not block unattended.

### The Solution

The entrypoint script (`docker-entrypoint.sh`) checks on startup:

1. **Does `/config/config.yaml` exist?**
   - **Yes** -- Start the server directly.
   - **No** -- Create a minimal config. The container starts, but without an
     LLM provider configured. API keys must be provided separately via
     `/config/.env` (Option A above).

2. **Does `/config/.env` exist?**
   - **No** -- Warning with instructions to add API keys.
   - **Yes** -- No action.

3. **Fallback (neither config nor .env):**
   The container exits with a clear error message and non-zero exit code.
   No stuck wizard.

### Container Commands

| Command | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `docker compose up -d` | Normal server operation |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | Interactive setup wizard (one-time) |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read config values |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell inside container |

## Health Check

A TCP connect check polls whether the Hermes server is listening on the
configured port:

```yaml
healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null"]
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 10s
  retries: 3
  start_period: 30s
```

Note: Hermes serve has no dedicated HTTP health endpoint. The TCP check is
a best-effort liveness signal -- a positive check means the port is open,
not necessarily that Hermes is fully initialised.

## Security

The container runs with restricted privileges:

- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable at build time)
- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true`
- **No unnecessary capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`
- **Write access only to:** `/config`, `/data/rw`, and optionally `/vault`
  (all mounted as volumes)

## Logging

```bash
docker compose logs -f
```

Hermes writes no persistent log files in serve mode (output goes to
stdout/stderr). For detailed diagnostics:

```bash
docker compose run --rm hermes doctor
```

## Backup

The only data that cannot be regenerated is the configuration:

```bash
tar czf hermes-config-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz hermes-config/
```

Restore:

```bash
tar xzf hermes-config-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Container exits immediately | Config missing | Create `./hermes-config/config.yaml` or run `hermes-init` |
| `hermes: command not found` | Build failure | `docker compose build --no-cache` |
| Cannot connect to server | Port not exposed | Check `docker compose ps`, fix port in `.env` |
| Permission denied on `/data/rw` | UID mismatch | Adjust build UID (see Permission Model) |
| "No API key configured" | `.env` missing or empty | Add API key to `./hermes-config/.env` |
| Vault not writable from inside | UID mismatch on vault files | Match `USER_ID` build arg to vault owner's UID |

## Known Limitations

- **No desktop app build inside container:** The desktop app (Electron) is
  not built inside the container. The `serve` command provides the
  JSON-RPC/WebSocket backend that desktop, TUI, or web clients connect to
  from outside.
- **Health check is TCP-only:** Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint.
- **`--insecure` is DEPRECATED:** Since the June 2026 hardening, binding on
  a public interface always requires an auth provider regardless of this
  flag. Use a tunnel (SSH/WireGuard) to 127.0.0.1 for local-only access.", "path": "/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker/README.md"}

{"success": true, "name": "hermes-agent", "file": "references/providers-and-models.md", "content": "# Providers & Model Aliases

Set via `hermes model` (picker) or `hermes setup`. 35+ provider profiles ship as
plugins under `plugins/model-providers/`; user plugins of the same name override.
Full docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers

### Providers

| Provider | Auth | Key env var(s) |
|----------|------|----------------|
| openrouter | API key | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| anthropic | API key | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (also `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) |
| nous | OAuth device code | `hermes auth add nous` (or `NOUS_API_KEY`) |
| openai-codex | OAuth | `hermes auth add openai-codex` |
| qwen-oauth | OAuth | `hermes auth add qwen-oauth` |
| minimax-oauth | OAuth | `hermes auth add minimax-oauth` |
| copilot | Token | `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` (Copilot device flow — `gh auth login` tokens do NOT work) |
| copilot-acp | External CLI | Copilot CLI on PATH or `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` |
| gemini | API key | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| xai | API key | `XAI_API_KEY` (SuperGrok OAuth also supported) |
| deepseek | API key | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| zai (GLM) | API key | `GLM_API_KEY` / `ZAI_API_KEY` |
| minimax / minimax-cn | API key | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` / `MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY` |
| kimi-coding / -cn | API key | `KIMI_API_KEY` / `KIMI_CN_API_KEY` |
| alibaba (+coding-plan) | API key | `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` / `ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| xiaomi | API key | `XIAOMI_API_KEY` |
| huggingface | Token | `HF_TOKEN` |
| fireworks / novita / nvidia / deepinfra / gmi / arcee / stepfun / upstage / kilocode / ai-gateway / opencode-zen / opencode-go / ollama-cloud | API key | `<NAME>_API_KEY` |
| bedrock / vertex / azure-foundry | Cloud SDK / key | AWS SDK creds / Vertex ADC / `AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY` |
| custom | Config | `model.base_url` + `model.api_key` in config.yaml |

Multiple credentials per provider pool and rotate automatically (`hermes auth`).
Fallback chain when the primary fails: `hermes fallback add|remove|list`.

### User-defined model aliases

Work with `/model <name>` in CLI and every gateway platform. Resolved by
`hermes_cli/model_switch.py::resolve_alias()`; user aliases are checked BEFORE
the built-in table, so a user `sonnet`/`grok` shadows the built-in.

```yaml
# Full form
model_aliases:
  fav:
    model: claude-sonnet-4.6
    provider: anthropic
  local-qwen:
    model: qwen3.5:397b
    provider: custom
    base_url: "https://ollama.com/v1"
  theta:
    model: theta-1
    provider: custom
    base_url: "https://theta.example.com/v1"
    key_env: THETA_API_KEY        # or: api_key: "${THETA_API_KEY}"

# Short form ("provider/model"), also via CLI:
#   hermes config set model.aliases.fav openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6
model:
  aliases:
    fav: openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6
```

`/model fav` — session-scoped; add `--global` to persist as default.

An alias with its own `base_url` authenticates with its own credential
(`api_key`, which also accepts a `"${VAR}"` reference, or `key_env`). With
neither set the key is resolved from the alias HOST, never carried over from
the provider that was active before the switch.

Built-in aliases (catalog-resolved against the active provider): `sonnet`,
`opus`, `haiku`, `claude`, `gpt5`, `gpt`, `codex`, `o3`, `o4`, `gemini`,
`deepseek`, `grok`, `llama`, `qwen`, `minimax`, `nemotron`, `kimi`, `glm`,
`step`, `mimo`, `trinity`.

{"success": true, "name": "hermes-agent", "file": "references/configuration.md", "content": "# Configuration, Toolsets & Voice

Edit with `hermes config edit` or `hermes config set section.key value`.
Full reference: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration

### Config Sections (most-used keys)

| Section | Key options |
|---------|-------------|
| `model` | `default`, `provider`, `base_url`, `api_key`, `context_length`, `aliases` |
| `agent` | `max_turns` (90), `tool_use_enforcement`, `service_tier`, `verify_on_stop` |
| `terminal` | `backend` (local/docker/ssh/modal/daytona/singularity), `cwd`, `timeout` (180) |
| `compression` | `enabled`, `threshold` (0.50), `target_ratio` (0.20) |
| `display` | `skin`, `interface` (cli/tui), `language`, `show_reasoning`, `show_cost`, `pet` |
| `approvals` | `mode` (smart/manual/off), `timeout`, `cron_mode` |
| `stt` | `enabled`, `provider` (local/groq/openai/mistral/elevenlabs/deepinfra) |
| `tts` | `provider` (edge/elevenlabs/openai/minimax/mistral/neutts/gemini/piper/kittentts/deepinfra/xai) |
| `memory` | `memory_enabled`, `user_profile_enabled`, `provider`, `write_approval` |
| `security` | `redact_secrets`, `tirith_enabled`, `website_blocklist` |
| `delegation` | `model`, `provider`, `max_concurrent_children`, `max_iterations` (50), `max_spawn_depth` |
| `checkpoints` | `enabled`, `max_snapshots` (50) |
| `curator` | `enabled`, `consolidate` (false, opt-in aux-model consolidation), `interval_hours`, `stale_after_days` |

`hermes config check` reports sections missing from an older config.

### Toolsets

Enable/disable via `hermes tools` (interactive) or `hermes tools enable/disable NAME`.
Full enumeration: `TOOLSETS` dict in `toolsets.py` (`_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS` is the default bundle most platforms inherit).

| Toolset | What it provides |
|---------|-----------------|
| `web` / `search` | Web search + extraction / search-only subset |
| `browser` | Browser automation (Browserbase, Camofox, or local Chromium) |
| `terminal` | Shell commands and process management |
| `file` | File read/write/search/patch |
| `code_execution` | Sandboxed Python execution |
| `coding` | Code-editing helpers (LSP-backed) |
| `computer_use` | Desktop GUI control (cua-driver) |
| `vision` | Image analysis |
| `image_gen` | Image generation and image-to-image editing |
| `video` / `video_gen` | Video analysis / video generation |
| `x_search` | X (Twitter) search (X OAuth or API key) |
| `tts` | Text-to-speech |
| `skills` | Skill browsing and management |
| `memory` | Persistent cross-session memory |
| `session_search` | Search past conversations |
| `context_engine` | Pluggable context-engine hooks |
| `project` | Named multi-folder workspace tools |
| `delegation` | Subagent task delegation |
| `cronjob` | Scheduled task management |
| `clarify` | Ask user clarifying questions |
| `todo` | In-session task planning |
| `kanban` | Multi-agent work-queue tools (gated to workers) |
| `debugging` | Extra introspection tools (off by default) |
| `safe` | Minimal low-risk toolset for locked-down sessions |
| `spotify`, `homeassistant`, `discord`, `discord_admin`, `feishu_doc`, `feishu_drive`, `yuanbao` | Service integrations (gated on their credentials) |

Tool changes take effect on `/reset` (new session) — never mid-conversation, to preserve prompt caching.

## Voice

### STT (Voice → Text)

Voice messages from messaging platforms are auto-transcribed.

```yaml
stt:
  enabled: true
  provider: local   # local (faster-whisper, free) | groq | openai | mistral | elevenlabs | deepinfra
  local:
    model: base     # tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3
```

Auto-detect priority: local faster-whisper (`pip install faster-whisper`) → Groq (`GROQ_API_KEY`, free tier) → OpenAI (`VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY`) → Mistral Voxtral (`MISTRAL_API_KEY`).

### TTS (Text → Voice)

| Provider | Env var | Free? |
|----------|---------|-------|
| Edge TTS (default) | None | Yes |
| ElevenLabs | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | Free tier |
| OpenAI | `VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY` | Paid |
| MiniMax | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` | Paid |
| Mistral | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` | Paid |
| Gemini | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Free tier |
| NeuTTS / Piper / KittenTTS (local) | None | Free |

Voice commands: `/voice on` (voice-to-voice), `/voice tts` (always voice), `/voice off`.

{"content": "# =============================================================================
# docker-compose.yml – Hermes Agent Container
# =============================================================================
# Quick start:
#   1. Pick a provider config from examples/ and copy to ./hermes-config/config.yaml
#   2. Add the matching API key to ./hermes-config/.env
#      (or run `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` once)
#   3. docker compose up -d
#   4. Connect your Hermes GUI client to http://host:8080
# =============================================================================
services:
  hermes:
    image: hermes-agent:latest
    build:
      context: .
      # Optional: pin a specific Hermes commit
      # args:
      #   HERMES_COMMIT: abc123def
    container_name: hermes
    restart: unless-stopped

    # ---- Port mapping ----
    ports:
      - "${HERMES_PORT:-8080}:${HERMES_PORT:-8080}"

    # ---- Volumes ----

{"content": "1|# Hermes Agent -- Docker
2|
3|Run [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) by **Nous Research**
4|inside a lean Debian container and connect from an external GUI client.
5|
6|## Architecture
7|
8|```
9|  +--------------------------------------------+
10|  |  Host                                      |
11|  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
12|  |  | ./input/         |-->| /data/ro       | |  Read-only input
13|  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |
14|  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
15|  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
16|  |  | ./workspace/     |<--| /data/rw       | |  Read-write work data
17|  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |
18|  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
19|  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
20|  |  | ./hermes-        |-->| /config        | |  Persistent config
21|  |  | config/          |   | (yaml + .env)  | |
22|  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
23|  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
24|  |  | /path/to/vault   |-->| /vault         | |  Optional Obsidian vault
25|  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |  (read-write, opt-in)
26|  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |
27|  |                                            |
28|  |  GUI client --port 8080--> container      |
29|  +--------------------------------------------+
30|```
31|
32|## Files
33|
34|| File | Purpose |
35||------|---------|
36|| `Dockerfile` | Multi-stage build (bookworm-slim) |
37|| `docker-compose.yml` | Service definition + init service |
38|| `docker-entrypoint.sh` | Config check, initialisation, server start |
39|| `.env.example` | Environment variable template (copy to `.env`) |
40|| `README.md` | This document |
41|
42|## Build
43|
44|```bash
45|docker compose build
46|```
47|
48|To pin a specific Hermes version, set `HERMES_COMMIT` in `.env` or pass it
49|as a build arg:
50|
51|```bash
52|docker compose build --build-arg HERMES_COMMIT=abc123def
53|```
54|
55|## Quick Start
56|
57|### 1. Provide Configuration
58|
59|**Option A -- Pre-made config (recommended for automation):**
60|
61|Create two files inside `./hermes-config/`:
62|
63|**`hermes-config/config.yaml`**:
64|```yaml
65|server:
66|  host: 0.0.0.0
67|  port: 8080
68|```
69|
70|**`hermes-config/.env`**:
71|```bash
72|# At least one LLM provider API key
73|OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...
74|```
75|
76|**Option B -- Interactive setup (run once):**
77|
78|```bash
79|docker compose run --rm hermes-init
80|```
81|
82|The wizard steps you through provider, model, and API key choices. The
83|generated config is saved to `./hermes-config/` and is picked up by the
84|regular service afterwards.
85|
86|### 2. Start
87|
88|```bash
89|docker compose up -d
90|```
91|
92|### 3. Connect
93|
94|Point your Hermes GUI client (desktop app) at:
95|
96|```
97|http://<host-ip>:8080
98|```
99|
100|## Port Configuration
101|
102|```bash
103|# Via .env
104|HERMES_PORT=9090
105|
106|# Or inline
107|HERMES_PORT=9090 docker compose up -d
108|```
109|
110|## Data Directories
111|
112|| Host path | Container | Mode | Purpose |
113||-----------|-----------|------|---------|
114|| `./input/` | `/data/ro` | `:ro` | Read-only host input data |
115|| `./workspace/` | `/data/rw` | `:rw` | Read-write work and results |
116|| `./hermes-config/` | `/config` | `:rw` | Persistent configuration + secrets |
117|| *(optional)* `/vault` | `/vault` | `:rw` | Optional Obsidian vault mount |
118|
119|## Optional Obsidian Vault Mount
120|
121|You can optionally mount an existing Obsidian vault into the container so
122|Hermes has read/write access to it -- the same freedom it has with its own
123|Hermes Vault (HV) in a non-Docker setup.
124|
125|This is **purely optional**. The container works perfectly without it.
126|
127|### How It Works
128|
129|- The vault is mounted at `/vault` inside the container.
130|- Hermes runs as the `hermes` user and has full r/w access to everything
131|  under `/vault`.
132|- The standard Hermes tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `search_files`,
133|  `patch`) work on `/vault/...` paths without extra configuration.
134|- Hermes can browse, create, and edit notes, search file contents, and
135|  manage markdown files -- everything it does with its own HV.
136|
137|### Setup
138|
139|Uncomment and adjust the vault volume in `docker-compose.yml`:
140|
141|```yaml
142|volumes:
143|  # ... other mounts ...
144|  - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw
145|```
146|
147|Replace the path with your actual vault location, for example:
148|
149|```yaml
150|  - /home/user/syncthing/obsidian-vault:/vault:rw
151|```
152|
153|### UID/GID Considerations
154|
155|The container user `hermes` has UID 1000 by default (configurable via build
156|args `USER_ID`/`GROUP_ID`). Your vault files must be readable and writable
157|by that UID. The two easiest approaches:
158|
159|1. **Match the build UID to your host user** (recommended):
160|   ```bash
161|   docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
162|   ```
163|
164|2. **Make vault files group-accessible**:
165|   ```bash
166|   chmod -R g+rws /path/to/your/vault
167|   ```
168|
169|### What Hermes Can Do With the Vault
170|
171|Once mounted, Hermes can perform all vault operations it normally does with
172|its own HV:
173|
174|| Operation | How |
175||-----------|-----|
176|| Read notes | `read_file(path="/vault/some-note.md")` |
177|| Write new notes | `write_file(path="/vault/new-note.md", content="...")` |
178|| Search contents | `search_files(pattern="...", path="/vault")` |
179|| Patch existing notes | `patch(path="/vault/some-note.md", old_string="...", new_string="...")` |
180|| Navigate directories | `terminal(command="ls /vault/")` |
181|| Create/manage markdown | All standard Hermes tools |
182|
183|The entrypoint script detects the vault mount on startup and reports
184|whether an Obsidian vault (`.obsidian/` marker) is present.
185|
186|## Permission Model (UID/GID)
187|
188|The Hermes process runs as user `hermes` (UID 1000 / GID 1000 by default).
189|
190|**If your host user has a different UID:**
191|
192|1. Check your UID:
193|   ```bash
194|   id -u
195|   ```
196|
197|2. Rebuild with matching UID:
198|   ```bash
199|   docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
200|   ```
201|
202|3. Ensure `./workspace/` is writable on the host:
203|   ```bash
204|   mkdir -p workspace input hermes-config
205|   chmod 755 workspace
206|   ```
207|
208|4. Or fix permissions after the first start:
209|   ```bash
210|   chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) workspace
211|   ```
212|
213|## Initialisation Strategy
214|
215|### The Problem
216|
217|`hermes setup` is an interactive wizard. In a headless container it must
218|not block unattended.
219|
220|### The Solution
221|
222|The entrypoint script (`docker-entrypoint.sh`) checks on startup:
223|
224|1. **Does `/config/config.yaml` exist?**
225|   - **Yes** -- Start the server directly.
226|   - **No** -- Create a minimal config. The container starts, but without an
227|     LLM provider configured. API keys must be provided separately via
228|     `/config/.env` (Option A above).
229|
230|2. **Does `/config/.env` exist?**
231|   - **No** -- Warning with instructions to add API keys.
232|   - **Yes** -- No action.
233|
234|3. **Fallback (neither config nor .env):**
235|   The container exits with a clear error message and non-zero exit code.
236|   No stuck wizard.
237|
238|### Container Commands
239|
240|| Command | Effect |
241||---------|--------|
242|| `docker compose up -d` | Normal server operation |
243|| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | Interactive setup wizard (one-time) |
244|| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read config values |
245|| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell inside container |
246|
247|## Health Check
248|
249|A TCP connect check polls whether the Hermes server is listening on the
250|configured port:
251|
252|```yaml
253|healthcheck:
254|  test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null"]
255|  interval: 30s
256|  timeout: 10s
257|  retries: 3
258|  start_period: 30s
259|```
260|
261|Note: Hermes serve has no dedicated HTTP health endpoint. The TCP check is
262|a best-effort liveness signal -- a positive check means the port is open,
263|not necessarily that Hermes is fully initialised.
264|
265|## Security
266|
267|The container runs with restricted privileges:
268|
269|- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable at build time)
270|- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true`
271|- **No unnecessary capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`
272|- **Write access only to:** `/config`, `/data/rw`, and optionally `/vault`
273|  (all mounted as volumes)
274|
275|## Logging
276|
277|```bash
278|docker compose logs -f
279|```
280|
281|Hermes writes no persistent log files in serve mode (output goes to
282|stdout/stderr). For detailed diagnostics:
283|
284|```bash
285|docker compose run --rm hermes doctor
286|```
287|
288|## Backup
289|
290|The only data that cannot be regenerated is the configuration:
291|
292|```bash
293|tar czf hermes-config-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz hermes-config/
294|```
295|
296|Restore:
297|
298|```bash
299|tar xzf hermes-config-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz
300|```
301|
302|## Troubleshooting
303|
304|| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
305||---------|-------|-----|
306|| Container exits immediately | Config missing | Create `./hermes-config/config.yaml` or run `hermes-init` |
307|| `hermes: command not found` | Build failure | `docker compose build --no-cache` |
308|| Cannot connect to server | Port not exposed | Check `docker compose ps`, fix port in `.env` |
309|| Permission denied on `/data/rw` | UID mismatch | Adjust build UID (see Permission Model) |
310|| "No API key configured" | `.env` missing or empty | Add API key to `./hermes-config/.env` |
311|| Vault not writable from inside | UID mismatch on vault files | Match `USER_ID` build arg to vault owner's UID |
312|
313|## Known Limitations
314|
315|- **No desktop app build inside container:** The desktop app (Electron) is
316|  not built inside the container. The `serve` command provides the
317|  JSON-RPC/WebSocket backend that desktop, TUI, or web clients connect to
318|  from outside.
319|- **Health check is TCP-only:** Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint.
320|- **`--insecure` is DEPRECATED:** Since the June 2026 hardening, binding on
321|  a public interface always requires an auth provider regardless of this
322|  flag. Use a tunnel (SSH/WireGuard) to 127.0.0.1 for local-only access.", "total_lines": 322, "file_size": 9533, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

model:

```bash
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...

model:
  default: openai/gpt-4o
  provider: openrouter

  host: 0.0.0.0

`deepseek/deepseek-chat`, `google/gemini-2.5-pro`.

Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint -- corporate API gateways,

```bash

model:

server:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: ${HERMES_PORT:-8080}
```

Replace the `base_url` and `api_key` values with your provider's actual
endpoint and credential.

{"content": "1|# =============================================================================
2|# Dockerfile – Hermes Agent (Debian Bookworm)
3|# =============================================================================
4|# Hermes Agent: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com
5|# Build: docker build -t hermes-agent:latest .
6|# =============================================================================
7|ARG DEBIAN_VERSION=bookworm
8|
9|FROM debian:${DEBIAN_VERSION}-slim AS build
10|
11|# ------------------------------------------------------------
12|# 1. System dependencies for the install script
13|# ------------------------------------------------------------
14|RUN set -eux; \
15|    apt-get update -qq; \
16|    apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
17|        ca-certificates \
18|        curl \
19|        git \
20|        ; \
21|    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
22|
23|# ------------------------------------------------------------
24|# 2. Install Hermes Agent (non-interactive)
25|# ------------------------------------------------------------
26|# Installs system-wide so the hermes binary is in PATH for any user.
27|# --non-interactive skips terminal-interactive stages.
28|ARG HERMES_BRANCH=main
29|ARG HERMES_COMMIT=""
30|
31|RUN set -eux; \
32|    INSTALL_ARGS=""; \
33|    if [ -n "${HERMES_COMMIT}" ]; then \
34|      INSTALL_ARGS="${INSTALL_ARGS} --commit ${HERMES_COMMIT}"; \
35|    fi; \
36|    curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh \
37|      | bash -s -- \
38|        --non-interactive \
39|        --branch "${HERMES_BRANCH}" \
40|        --dir /opt/hermes-agent \
41|        ${INSTALL_ARGS} \
42|        ; \
43|    /opt/hermes-agent/bin/hermes --version
44|
45|# =============================================================================
46|# Runtime stage — smaller final image, no build-time dependencies
47|# =============================================================================
48|FROM debian:${DEBIAN_VERSION}-slim
49|
50|# ------------------------------------------------------------
51|# 1. Runtime system dependencies
52|# ------------------------------------------------------------
53|RUN set -eux; \
54|    apt-get update -qq; \
55|    apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
56|        ca-certificates \
57|        git \
58|        ; \
59|    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
60|
61|# ------------------------------------------------------------
62|# 2. Copy Hermes from build stage
63|# ------------------------------------------------------------
64|COPY --from=build /opt/hermes-agent /opt/hermes-agent
65|RUN ln -s /opt/hermes-agent/bin/hermes /usr/local/bin/hermes
66|
67|# ------------------------------------------------------------
68|# 3. Create non-root user
69|# ------------------------------------------------------------
70|# UID/GID can be overridden at build time to match the host user.
71|ARG USER_ID=1000
72|ARG GROUP_ID=1000
73|
74|RUN set -eux; \
75|    groupadd --gid "${GROUP_ID}" --non-unique hermes; \
76|    useradd  --uid "${USER_ID}" --gid "${GROUP_ID}" \
77|             --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin \
78|             hermes; \
79|    install -d -o hermes -g hermes -m 0755 \
80|        /config \
81|        /data/rw \
82|        /vault \
83|        /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes
84|
85|# ------------------------------------------------------------
86|# 4. Volumes & environment
87|# ------------------------------------------------------------
88|# Persistent Hermes configuration (mount or named volume).
89|VOLUME /config
90|
91|# Optional Obsidian vault mount for Hermes to read/write freely.
92|VOLUME /vault
93|
94|# Read-only input data from host.
95|VOLUME /data/ro
96|
97|# Read-write working data from host.
98|VOLUME /data/rw
99|
100|ENV HERMES_HOME=/config
101|ENV HERMES_PORT=8080
102|
103|EXPOSE ${HERMES_PORT}
104|
105|# ------------------------------------------------------------
106|# 5. Entrypoint
107|# ------------------------------------------------------------
108|WORKDIR /data/rw
109|USER hermes
110|
111|COPY --chown=hermes:hermes docker-entrypoint.sh /docker-entrypoint.sh
112|RUN chmod 755 /docker-entrypoint.sh
113|
114|ENTRYPOINT ["/docker-entrypoint.sh"]

```

```

But the permission issue is the real problem. Let me fix the Dockerfile to make sure the `.hermes` tools are accessible to the `hermes` user.

{"new_string": "# The 'hermes' launcher was copied into /opt/hermes-agent/bin/ during build.
# It hardcodes the hermetic tools python without the venv site-packages.

    \
    # Find the venv python (the one with all dependencies installed) \
    VENV_PY=$(find /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/installs -name "python3" -path "*/venv/bin/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1); \
    if [ -n "$VENV_PY" ]; then \
        echo "Using venv python: $VENV_PY"; \
        HERMES_SOURCE="/opt/hermes-agent"; \
        cat > /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes << 'HERMESWRAP'
#!/bin/sh
# Hermes launcher wrapper — finds and runs the correct Python with venv
VENV_PY="$(find /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/installs -name "python3" -path "*/venv/bin/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -z "$VENV_PY" ]; then
    VENV_PY="$(find /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/tools -name "python3" -path "*/bin/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
fi
export PYTHONPATH="/opt/hermes-agent${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
exec "$VENV_PY" -I -c "
import os, re, sys
os.environ.pop('PYTHONHOME', None)
os.environ.pop('PYTHONPATH', None)
sys.path.insert(0, '/opt/hermes-agent')

for sp in glob.glob('/opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/installs/*/environments/*/venv/lib/python*/site-packages'):

from hermes_cli.main import main
sys.argv[0] = re.sub(r'(-script\.pyw|\.exe)?$', '', sys.argv[0])
sys.exit(main())
" "$@"

# =============================================================================
# generate-password-hash.sh -- Generate a Hermes password hash for basic auth
# =============================================================================
# Usage:
#   docker compose build   # one-time
#   ./generate-password-hash.sh [password]
#

# =============================================================================

PASSWORD="${1:-demo}"

{"new_string": "## Known Limitations

- **No desktop app build inside container:** The desktop app (Electron) is
  not built inside the container. The `serve` command provides the
  JSON-RPC/WebSocket backend that desktop, TUI, or web clients connect to
  from outside.
- **Health check is TCP-only:** Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint.

## "Refusing to bind dashboard to 0.0.0.0" — Workaround

Since the June 2026 hardening, Hermes refuses to bind `serve` to `0.0.0.0`
(all interfaces) without a configured auth provider. This is by design —
anyone who reaches the port would have full access to Hermes.

You have three options:

### Option 1: Password auth (recommended)

Add this block to your `config.yaml`:

```yaml
dashboard:
  basic_auth:
    username: admin
    password_hash: "scrypt$16384$8$1$..."
```

The password hash is scrypt-based. Generate one for your own password:

```bash
# Using the built image:
./generate-password-hash.sh my-secret-password

# Or with docker directly:
docker run --rm --entrypoint bash hermes-agent:latest -c '
  python3 -c "
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, \"/opt/hermes-agent\")
import glob
for sp in glob.glob(\"/opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/installs/*/environments/*/venv/lib/python*/site-packages\"):
    sys.path.insert(0, sp)
from plugins.dashboard_auth.basic import hash_password
print(hash_password(\"my-secret-password\"))
  "
'
```

All example configs in `examples/` include a `dashboard.basic_auth` block with
a demo password (`admin` / `demo`). Change it before exposing to a network.

### Option 2: SSH tunnel (no auth needed)

Bind the server to `127.0.0.1` (local container only) and tunnel from your
client machine:

```yaml
# in config.yaml — bind only inside the container
server:
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8080
```

```bash
# On your client machine — tunnel to the container host
ssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 user@container-host
```

Then connect your GUI client to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` on the client machine.

### Option 3: WireGuard tunnel (no auth needed)

Same principle as SSH, but with WireGuard: bind to `127.0.0.1` and let
WireGuard forward the port. This is the approach Hermes docs recommend:

```
Bind 127.0.0.1 + tunnel to keep it local.

## Workaround — bind to 0.0.0.0

Drei Wege, der erste ist für deinen Docker-Einsatz der richtige:

### 1. Password-Auth (empfohlen)

Füge in `config.yaml` einen `dashboard.basic_auth`-Block ein. Alle drei Beispiel-Configs in `examples/` haben ihn jetzt schon mit einem Demo-Passwort (`admin` / `demo`).

### 2. SSH-Tunnel (kein Auth nötig)

{"content": "# =============================================================================
# hermes-docker.service -- systemd user service
# =============================================================================
# Starts the Hermes container on login, stops it on logout.
#
# Install:
#   mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user/
#   cp hermes-docker.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
#   systemctl --user daemon-reload
#   systemctl --user enable hermes-docker
#   systemctl --user start hermes-docker
#
# Check status:
#   systemctl --user status hermes-docker
#   journalctl --user -u hermes-docker -f
#
# Remove:
#   systemctl --user stop hermes-docker
#   systemctl --user disable hermes-docker
#   rm ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service
#   systemctl --user daemon-reload
# =============================================================================

[Unit]
Description=Hermes Agent Docker Container
Documentation=https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com
Requires=docker.service
After=docker.service network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes

# Path to your project directory -- adjust if different
WorkingDirectory=%h/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker

ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d
ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker compose -f docker-compose.yml down

# Stop timeout: give Hermes 30s to shut down gracefully
ExecStop=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/docker compose -f docker-compose.yml down --timeout 30'

# Restart on failure (e.g. after Docker daemon restart)
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target", "path": "/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker/hermes-docker.service"}

The user wants:
1. Everything finalized and documented so they can set it up and use it easily
2. An autostart mechanism: container starts on login, stops on logout

Let me think about what needs to be done:

1. **Finalize everything** - make sure all files are consistent, the build works, and documentation is complete
2. **Autostart system** - For Linux, the best approach would be:
   - Systemd user service (starts on user login, stops on logout)
   - Or a simple script in ~/.config/autostart/ for desktop environments
   - Or adding commands to ~/.bashrc / ~/.bash_profile / ~/.bash_logout

Since the user mentioned "bei jeder Anmeldung am Rechner" (on login) and "beim ABMELDEN BEENDET" (on logout), this sounds like they want it tied to their user session. On Linux with a desktop environment, the cleanest approaches are:

1. **systemd --user service**: Starts when the user logs in (via PAM or display manager), stops when the user logs out. Best for terminal/server use.

{"content": "# Hermes Agent -- Docker

Run [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) by **Nous Research**
inside a lean Debian container and connect from an external GUI client.

## Project Files

```
hermes-inside-docker/
|-- Dockerfile                    Multi-stage build (bookworm-slim)
|-- docker-compose.yml            Service + init service definition
|-- docker-entrypoint.sh          Config check, initialisation, server start
|-- hermes-launcher.sh            Wrapper that finds the venv Python at runtime
|-- hermes-docker.service         systemd --user autostart (login = start, logout = stop)
|-- generate-password-hash.sh     Helper: generate a bcrypt password hash
|-- .env.example                  Environment variable template (copy to .env)
|-- README.md                     This document
|-- examples/
|   |-- config.openai.yaml        Config for OpenAI
|   |-- config.openrouter.yaml    Config for OpenRouter
|   +-- config.custom-openai.yaml Config for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
```

## Quick Start (5 minutes)

### 1. Build the Image

```bash
cd hermes-inside-docker
docker compose build
```

This takes 3-5 minutes on first run (downloads Debian packages, clones Hermes,
installs Python dependencies, builds the web UI). Subsequent builds are cached.

### 2. Configure

Choose a provider and copy the matching example config:

```bash
# Option A: OpenAI
cp examples/config.openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml

# Option B: OpenRouter
cp examples/config.openrouter.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml

# Option C: Custom OpenAI-compatible (corporate API, self-hosted vLLM, etc.)
cp examples/config.custom-openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml

# Option D: Interactive wizard (one-time)
# docker compose run --rm hermes-init
```

### 3. Set API Keys

Create `hermes-config/.env` with your API key:

```bash
# OpenAI
echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-..." > hermes-config/.env

# Or OpenRouter
echo "OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-..." > hermes-config/.env

# Or custom provider
echo "CUSTOM_API_KEY=sk-..." > hermes-config/.env
```

### 4. (Important) Set a Password

The Hermes server binds to `0.0.0.0` (all network interfaces). Since the
June 2026 hardening, this requires an auth provider. The example configs
include a demo password (`admin` / `demo`). **Change it immediately:**

```bash
# Generate a hash for your own password:
./generate-password-hash.sh your-secure-password
```

Copy the output into `hermes-config/config.yaml` under `dashboard.basic_auth`.

### 5. Start the Server

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

### 6. Connect

Point your Hermes GUI client (desktop app, web dashboard, or any JSON-RPC
compatible client) at:

```
http://<host-ip>:8080
```

Your browser will ask for the username and password configured in step 4.

---

## Detailed Guide

### Provider Configuration

All example configs are in `examples/`. Each sets the model provider and
includes a password auth block. Pick one:

| File | Provider | API Key Env Var |
|------|----------|-----------------|
| `config.openai.yaml` | OpenAI (`openai`) | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `config.openrouter.yaml` | OpenRouter (`openrouter`) | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `config.custom-openai.yaml` | Custom (`custom` + `base_url`) | `CUSTOM_API_KEY` |

**Custom provider (e.g. corporate API gateway):**

Edit `examples/config.custom-openai.yaml` and set the `base_url` to your
provider's endpoint:

```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-4o-mini
  provider: custom
  base_url: "https://api.your-company.com/v1"
  api_key: "${CUSTOM_API_KEY}"
```

### Auth: Three Ways to Handle 0.0.0.0 Binding

The Hermes server refuses to bind to `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) without
authentication. Choose one:

#### A) Password Auth (recommended)

Already included in all example configs. Generate your own hash:

```bash
./generate-password-hash.sh my-password
```

Output:
```
dashboard:
  basic_auth:
    username: admin
    password_hash: "scrypt$16384$8$1$..."
```

Paste this block into `hermes-config/config.yaml`.

#### B) SSH Tunnel (no auth)

Bind to `127.0.0.1` in config.yaml:

```yaml
server:
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8080
```

Tunnel from your client machine:

```bash
ssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 user@docker-host
```

Then connect to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` on your client.

#### C) WireGuard Tunnel (no auth)

Same principle: bind to `127.0.0.1`, forward the port through WireGuard.

### Data Directories

| Host Path | Container Path | Mode | Purpose |
|-----------|---------------|------|---------|
| `./input/` | `/data/ro` | `:ro` | Read-only input data from host |
| `./workspace/` | `/data/rw` | `:rw` | Read-write work and results |
| `./hermes-config/` | `/config` | `:rw` | Persistent config (yaml + .env) |
| *(optional)* | `/vault` | `:rw` | Obsidian vault (opt-in, see below) |

### Optional Obsidian Vault Mount

Mount an existing Obsidian vault so Hermes can read, write, search, and
patch notes -- the same full access it has with its own HV.

Uncomment the vault volume in `docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
volumes:
  - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw
```

Hermes detects the mount on startup and logs whether it contains an
`.obsidian/` marker. All Hermes tools (`read_file`, `write_file`,
`search_files`, `patch`) work on `/vault/...` paths without extra config.

### Permission Model (UID/GID)

The container user `hermes` has UID 1000 / GID 1000 by default. If your
host user has a different UID, rebuild:

```bash
docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
```

### Container Commands

| Command | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `docker compose up -d` | Start server in background |
| `docker compose down` | Stop server |
| `docker compose logs -f` | Follow log output |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | Interactive setup wizard (one-time) |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read a config value |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell inside container |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes doctor` | Hermes diagnostics |

---

## Autostart: Start on Login, Stop on Logout

The project includes a **systemd --user service** that:
- **Starts** the Hermes container when you log in
- **Stops** it when you log out
- **Restarts** it automatically if it crashes

### Prerequisites

- `systemd --user` must be available (default on most Linux distributions
  with GNOME, KDE, or similar desktop environments)
- Docker must be installed and running

### Installation

```bash
# 1. Copy the service file to your user systemd directory
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user/
cp hermes-docker.service ~/.config/systemd/user/

# 2. Edit the path in the service file to match your project location
nano ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service
# Change "WorkingDirectory=%h/..." to the actual absolute path of your
# hermes-inside-docker directory, for example:
#   WorkingDirectory=/home/rb/hermes-inside-docker
#
# %h expands to your home directory at runtime. Use the full path if
# your project is outside your home.

# 3. Reload systemd, enable, and start
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable hermes-docker
systemctl --user start hermes-docker
```

### Verification

```bash
# Check if it's running
systemctl --user status hermes-docker

# Watch logs
journalctl --user -u hermes-docker -f

# Test the lifecycle: log out and back in, then check
systemctl --user status hermes-docker
# Should show "active (exited)" after login
```

### How It Works

- `WantedBy=default.target` tells systemd to start this service whenever
  the user session starts (i.e., on login).
- `Type=oneshot` + `RemainAfterExit=yes` means the service runs the start
  command, records itself as active, and runs the stop command when stopped.
- When the user logs out, systemd --user terminates, which stops all user
  services including this one.
- `Restart=on-failure` ensures the container restarts if Docker restarts
  or the container crashes.

### Uninstall

```bash
systemctl --user stop hermes-docker
systemctl --user disable hermes-docker
rm ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service
systemctl --user daemon-reload
```

### Alternative: Desktop Autostart (no systemd)

If your system doesn't use systemd --user, create a desktop autostart entry:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/autostart/
cat > ~/.config/autostart/hermes-docker.desktop << 'EOF'
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=Hermes Agent Docker
Comment=Start Hermes container on login
Exec=docker compose -f /path/to/hermes-inside-docker/docker-compose.yml up -d
Terminal=false
X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true
EOF
```

And a logout script to stop it:

```bash
cat > ~/.config/autostart/hermes-docker-stop.desktop << 'EOF'
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=Hermes Agent Stop
Comment=Stop Hermes container on logout
Exec=docker compose -f /path/to/hermes-inside-docker/docker-compose.yml down
Terminal=false
X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true
EOF
```

---

## Security

- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable at build time)
- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true` in compose
- **No unnecessary capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`
- **Write access only to:** `/config`, `/data/rw`, and optionally `/vault`
  (all mounted volumes)
- **Auth required for public bind:** Password or OAuth since June 2026 hardening

## Health Check

```yaml
healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null"]
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 10s
  retries: 3
  start_period: 30s
```

This is a TCP connect check (Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint).

## Backup

```bash
tar czf hermes-config-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz hermes-config/
```

Restore:

```bash
tar xzf hermes-config-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Container exits immediately | Config missing | Create `./hermes-config/config.yaml` or run `hermes-init` |
| `hermes: command not found` | Build failure | `docker compose build --no-cache` |
| Cannot connect to server | Port not exposed | Check `docker compose ps`, fix port in `.env` |
| Permission denied on `/data/rw` | UID mismatch | Rebuild with `USER_ID=$(id -u)` |
| "No API key configured" | `.env` missing or empty | Add API key to `./hermes-config/.env` |
| Vault not writable | UID mismatch on vault files | Match `USER_ID` build arg to vault owner |
| Server refuses to bind 0.0.0.0 | Auth not configured | Add `dashboard.basic_auth` to config.yaml (see Auth section) |
| systemd service won't start | Path wrong in service file | Edit `WorkingDirectory` in `~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service` |

## Known Limitations

- **No desktop app build:** The Electron desktop app is not built inside
  the container. `hermes serve` provides the JSON-RPC/WebSocket backend.
- **Health check is TCP-only:** No HTTP health endpoint.
- **Large image:** ~4.2 GB (includes Hermes' bundled tools: ffmpeg, node,
  Python, browser agent, etc.). This is normal for a Hermes installation.
- **Memory:** Expect ~200-400 MB RAM usage when idle.", "path": "/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker/README.md"}

116|Add to `hermes-config/.env`:
117|```bash
118|OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...
119|```
120|
121|**config.openai.yaml** (full file in `examples/`):
122|```yaml
123|model:
124|  default: gpt-4o
125|  provider: openai
126|server:
127|  host: 0.0.0.0
128|  port: ${HERMES_PORT:-8080}
129|```
130|
131|### OpenRouter
132|
133|OpenRouter hosts models from many providers. Use the `provider/model` notation:
134|
135|```bash
136|cp examples/config.openrouter.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml
137|```
138|
139|Add to `hermes-config/.env`:
140|```bash
141|OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...
142|```
143|
144|**config.openrouter.yaml** (full file in `examples/`):
145|```yaml
146|model:
147|  default: openai/gpt-4o
148|  provider: openrouter
149|server:
150|  host: 0.0.0.0
151|  port: ${HERMES_PORT:-8080}
152|```
153|
154|Other model examples for OpenRouter: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`,
155|`deepseek/deepseek-chat`, `google/gemini-2.5-pro`.
156|
157|### Custom OpenAI-Compatible Provider (Corporate API, Self-Hosted)
158|
159|Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint -- corporate API gateways,
160|self-hosted vLLM/TGI, or local proxies. Use the `custom` provider type with
161|a `base_url`:
162|
163|```bash
164|cp examples/config.custom-openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml
165|```
166|
167|Add to `hermes-config/.env`:
168|```bash
169|CUSTOM_API_KEY=sk-...
170|```
171|
172|**config.custom-openai.yaml** (full file in `examples/`):
173|```yaml
174|model:
175|  default: gpt-4o-mini
176|  provider: custom
177|  base_url: "https://api.your-company.com/v1"
178|  api_key: "${CUSTOM_API_KEY}"
179|server:
180|  host: 0.0.0.0
181|  port: ${HERMES_PORT:-8080}
182|```
183|
184|Replace the `base_url` and `api_key` values with your provider's actual
185|endpoint and credential.
186|
187|## Port Configuration
188|
189|```bash
190|# Via .env
191|HERMES_PORT=9090
192|
193|# Or inline
194|HERMES_PORT=9090 docker compose up -d
195|```
196|
197|## Data Directories
198|
199|| Host path | Container | Mode | Purpose |
200||-----------|-----------|------|---------|
201|| `./input/` | `/data/ro` | `:ro` | Read-only host input data |
202|| `./workspace/` | `/data/rw` | `:rw` | Read-write work and results |
203|| `./hermes-config/` | `/config` | `:rw` | Persistent configuration + secrets |
204|| *(optional)* `/vault` | `/vault` | `:rw` | Optional Obsidian vault mount |
205|
206|## Optional Obsidian Vault Mount
207|
208|You can optionally mount an existing Obsidian vault into the container so
209|Hermes has read/write access to it -- the same freedom it has with its own
210|Hermes Vault (HV) in a non-Docker setup.
211|
212|This is **purely optional**. The container works perfectly without it.
213|
214|### How It Works
215|
216|- The vault is mounted at `/vault` inside the container.
217|- Hermes runs as the `hermes` user and has full r/w access to everything
218|  under `/vault`.
219|- The standard Hermes tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `search_files`,
220|  `patch`) work on `/vault/...` paths without extra configuration.
221|- Hermes can browse, create, and edit notes, search file contents, and
222|  manage markdown files -- everything it does with its own HV.
223|
224|### Setup
225|
226|Uncomment and adjust the vault volume in `docker-compose.yml`:
227|
228|```yaml
229|volumes:
230|  # ... other mounts ...
231|  - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw
232|```
233|
234|Replace the path with your actual vault location, for example:
235|
236|```yaml
237|  - /home/user/syncthing/obsidian-vault:/vault:rw
238|```
239|
240|### UID/GID Considerations
241|
242|The container user `hermes` has UID 1000 by default (configurable via build
243|args `USER_ID`/`GROUP_ID`). Your vault files must be readable and writable
244|by that UID. The two easiest approaches:
245|
246|1. **Match the build UID to your host user** (recommended):
247|   ```bash
248|   docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
249|   ```
250|
251|2. **Make vault files group-accessible**:
252|   ```bash
253|   chmod -R g+rws /path/to/your/vault
254|   ```
255|
256|### What Hermes Can Do With the Vault
257|
258|Once mounted, Hermes can perform all vault operations it normally does with
259|its own HV:
260|
261|| Operation | How |
262||-----------|-----|
263|| Read notes | `read_file(path="/vault/some-note.md")` |
264|| Write new notes | `write_file(path="/vault/new-note.md", content="...")` |
265|| Search contents | `search_files(pattern="...", path="/vault")` |
266|| Patch existing notes | `patch(path="/vault/some-note.md", old_string="...", new_string="...")` |
267|| Navigate directories | `terminal(command="ls /vault/")` |
268|| Create/manage markdown | All standard Hermes tools |
269|
270|The entrypoint script detects the vault mount on startup and reports
271|whether an Obsidian vault (`.obsidian/` marker) is present.
272|
273|## Permission Model (UID/GID)
274|
275|The Hermes process runs as user `hermes` (UID 1000 / GID 1000 by default).
276|
277|**If your host user has a different UID:**
278|
279|1. Check your UID:
280|   ```bash
281|   id -u
282|   ```
283|
284|2. Rebuild with matching UID:
285|   ```bash
286|   docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
287|   ```
288|
289|3. Ensure `./workspace/` is writable on the host:
290|   ```bash
291|   mkdir -p workspace input hermes-config
292|   chmod 755 workspace
293|   ```
294|
295|4. Or fix permissions after the first start:
296|   ```bash
297|   chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) workspace
298|   ```
299|
300|## Initialisation Strategy
301|
302|### The Problem
303|
304|`hermes setup` is an interactive wizard. In a headless container it must
305|not block unattended.
306|
307|### The Solution
308|
309|The entrypoint script (`docker-entrypoint.sh`) checks on startup:
310|
311|1. **Does `/config/config.yaml` exist?**
312|   - **Yes** -- Start the server directly.
313|   - **No** -- Create a minimal config. The container starts, but without an
314|     LLM provider configured. API keys must be provided separately via
315|     `/config/.env` (Option A above).
316|
317|2. **Does `/config/.env` exist?**
318|   - **No** -- Warning with instructions to add API keys.
319|   - **Yes** -- No action.
320|
321|3. **Fallback (neither config nor .env):**
322|   The container exits with a clear error message and non-zero exit code.
323|   No stuck wizard.
324|
325|### Container Commands
326|
327|| Command | Effect |
328||---------|--------|
329|| `docker compose up -d` | Normal server operation |
330|| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | Interactive setup wizard (one-time) |
331|| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read config values |
332|| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell inside container |
333|
334|## Health Check
335|
336|A TCP connect check polls whether the Hermes server is listening on the
337|configured port:
338|
339|```yaml
340|healthcheck:
341|  test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null"]
342|  interval: 30s
343|  timeout: 10s
344|  retries: 3
345|  start_period: 30s
346|```
347|
348|Note: Hermes serve has no dedicated HTTP health endpoint. The TCP check is
349|a best-effort liveness signal -- a positive check means the port is open,
350|not necessarily that Hermes is fully initialised.
351|
352|## Security
353|
354|The container runs with restricted privileges:
355|
356|- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable at build time)
357|- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true`
358|- **No unnecessary capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`
359|- **Write access only to:** `/config`, `/data/rw`, and optionally `/vault`
360|  (all mounted as volumes)
361|
362|## Logging
363|
364|```bash
365|docker compose logs -f
366|```
367|
368|Hermes writes no persistent log files in serve mode (output goes to
369|stdout/stderr). For detailed diagnostics:
370|
371|```bash
372|docker compose run --rm hermes doctor
373|```
374|
375|## Backup
376|
377|The only data that cannot be regenerated is the configuration:
378|
379|```bash
380|tar czf hermes-config-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz hermes-config/
381|```
382|
383|Restore:
384|
385|```bash
386|tar xzf hermes-config-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz
387|```
388|
389|## Troubleshooting
390|
391|| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
392||---------|-------|-----|
393|| Container exits immediately | Config missing | Create `./hermes-config/config.yaml` or run `hermes-init` |
394|| `hermes: command not found` | Build failure | `docker compose build --no-cache` |
395|| Cannot connect to server | Port not exposed | Check `docker compose ps`, fix port in `.env` |
396|| Permission denied on `/data/rw` | UID mismatch | Adjust build UID (see Permission Model) |
397|| "No API key configured" | `.env` missing or empty | Add API key to `./hermes-config/.env` |
398|| Vault not writable from inside | UID mismatch on vault files | Match `USER_ID` build arg to vault owner's UID |
399|
400|## Known Limitations
401|
402|- **No desktop app build inside container:** The desktop app (Electron) is
403|  not built inside the container. The `serve` command provides the
404|  JSON-RPC/WebSocket backend that desktop, TUI, or web clients connect to
405|  from outside.
406|- **Health check is TCP-only:** Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint.
407|
408|## "Refusing to bind dashboard to 0.0.0.0" — Workaround
409|
410|Since the June 2026 hardening, Hermes refuses to bind `serve` to `0.0.0.0`
411|(all interfaces) without a configured auth provider. This is by design —
412|anyone who reaches the port would have full access to Hermes.
413|
414|You have three options:
415|
416|### Option 1: Password auth (recommended)
417|
418|Add this block to your `config.yaml`:
419|
420|```yaml
421|dashboard:
422|  basic_auth:
423|    username: admin
424|    password_hash: "scrypt$16384$8$1$..."
425|```
426|
427|The password hash is scrypt-based. Generate one for your own password:
428|
429|```bash
430|# Using the built image:
431|./generate-password-hash.sh my-secret-password
432|
433|# Or with docker directly:
434|docker run --rm --entrypoint bash hermes-agent:latest -c '
435|  python3 -c "
436|import sys
437|sys.path.insert(0, \"/opt/hermes-agent\")
438|import glob
439|for sp in glob.glob(\"/opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/installs/*/environments/*/venv/lib/python*/site-packages\"):
440|    sys.path.insert(0, sp)
441|from plugins.dashboard_auth.basic import hash_password
442|print(hash_password(\"my-secret-password\"))
443|  "
444|'
445|```
446|
447|All example configs in `examples/` include a `dashboard.basic_auth` block with
448|a demo password (`admin` / `demo`). Change it before exposing to a network.
449|
450|### Option 2: SSH tunnel (no auth needed)
451|
452|Bind the server to `127.0.0.1` (local container only) and tunnel from your
453|client machine:
454|
455|```yaml
456|# in config.yaml — bind only inside the container
457|server:
458|  host: 127.0.0.1
459|  port: 8080
460|```
461|
462|```bash
463|# On your client machine — tunnel to the container host
464|ssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 user@container-host
465|```
466|
467|Then connect your GUI client to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` on the client machine.
468|
469|### Option 3: WireGuard tunnel (no auth needed)
470|
471|Same principle as SSH, but with WireGuard: bind to `127.0.0.1` and let
472|WireGuard forward the port. This is the approach Hermes docs recommend:
473|
474|```
475|Bind 127.0.0.1 + tunnel to keep it local.
476|```
477|- **`--insecure` is DEPRECATED:** Since the June 2026 hardening, binding on
478|  a public interface always requires an auth provider regardless of this
