{"content": "# Hermes Agent -- Docker

Run [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) by **Nous Research**
inside a Debian container and connect from an external GUI client.

## Project Files

```
hermes-inside-docker/
  Dockerfile                    Multi-stage build (bookworm-slim)
  docker-compose.yml            Service + init service definition
  docker-entrypoint.sh          Config check, initialisation, server start
  hermes-launcher.sh            Wrapper that finds the venv Python at runtime
  hermes-docker.service         systemd --user autostart (login=start, logout=stop)
  generate-password-hash.sh     Helper: generate an scrypt password hash
  .env.example                  Environment variable template
  README.md                     This document
  examples/
    config.openai.yaml          Config + password auth for OpenAI
    config.openrouter.yaml      Config + password auth for OpenRouter
    config.custom-openai.yaml   Config + password auth for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
```

## Architecture

```
  Host
   +-------+    /data/ro (ro)        Read-only input data
   | input |----> container
   +-------+    /data/rw (rw)        Read-write work and results
   |workspc|----> container
   +-------+    /config (rw)         Persistent config (yaml + .env)
   |config |----> container
   +-------+    /vault (rw)          Optional Obsidian vault (opt-in)
   | vault |----> container
   +-------+
        GUI client --port 8080--> container
```

---

## Quick Start -- 5 Minutes

### 1. Build

```bash
cd hermes-inside-docker
docker compose build
```

Takes 3-5 min on first run. Subsequent builds are instant (cached).

### 2. Configure

Pick your LLM provider and copy the matching config:

```bash
# OpenAI
cp examples/config.openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml

# OpenRouter
cp examples/config.openrouter.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml

# Corporate / self-hosted OpenAI-compatible API
cp examples/config.custom-openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml
```

### 3. Set API Key

```bash
# OpenAI
echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-..." > hermes-config/.env

# OpenRouter
echo "OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-..." > hermes-config/.env

# Custom
echo "CUSTOM_API_KEY=sk-..." > hermes-config/.env
```

### 4. Change Default Password (Important)

The example configs include a demo password: **username `admin`, password `demo`**.
Generate your own:

```bash
./generate-password-hash.sh your-secure-password
```

Replace the `password_hash` value in `hermes-config/config.yaml` with the output.

### 5. Start

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

### 6. Connect

Point your Hermes GUI client to:

```
http://<host-ip>:8080
```

Enter the username and password from step 4.

---

## Provider Configuration

### OpenAI

```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-4o
  provider: openai
```
| Env var: `OPENAI_API_KEY`

### OpenRouter

```yaml
model:
  default: openai/gpt-4o
  provider: openrouter
```
| Env var: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`

Other models: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`, `deepseek/deepseek-chat`,
`google/gemini-2.5-pro`.

### Custom OpenAI-Compatible

```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-4o-mini
  provider: custom
  base_url: "https://api.your-company.com/v1"
  api_key: "${CUSTOM_API_KEY}"
```
| Env var: `CUSTOM_API_KEY`

Works with corporate API gateways, self-hosted vLLM/TGI, or local proxies.

### Interactive Setup (Alternative)

```bash
docker compose run --rm hermes-init
```

Runs the Hermes setup wizard interactively. Generated config is saved to
`./hermes-config/`.

---

## Auth -- Required for 0.0.0.0 Binding

Since June 2026, Hermes refuses to bind `serve` to `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces)
without an auth provider. You have three options:

| Option | Auth needed | External access |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| A. Password auth | yes | direct |
| B. SSH tunnel | no | via tunnel |
| C. WireGuard tunnel | no | via tunnel |

### A) Password Auth (Recommended)

All example configs include a `dashboard.basic_auth` block. Generate your own:

```bash
./generate-password-hash.sh my-password
```

Output:
```
dashboard:
  basic_auth:
    username: admin
    password_hash: "scrypt$16384$8$1$..."
```

Paste into `hermes-config/config.yaml`.

### B) SSH Tunnel (No Auth)

```yaml
server:
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8080
```

```bash
ssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 user@docker-host
# Then connect to http://127.0.0.1:8080 from client machine
```

### C) WireGuard Tunnel (No Auth)

Same as SSH: bind to `127.0.0.1`, forward via WireGuard.

---

## Port

```bash
# Via .env
HERMES_PORT=9090

# Inline
HERMES_PORT=9090 docker compose up -d
```

Default: 8080.

---

## Data Directories

| Host path | Container | Mode | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------|------|---------|
| `./input/` | `/data/ro` | `:ro` | Read-only input from host |
| `./workspace/` | `/data/rw` | `:rw` | Read-write work and results |
| `./hermes-config/` | `/config` | `:rw` | Persistent configuration + API keys |
| *(optional)* `/vault` | `/vault` | `:rw` | Obsidian vault (opt-in below) |

---

## Optional Obsidian Vault Mount

Mount an existing Obsidian vault so Hermes can read, write, search, and
patch notes -- same full access as with its own HV.

### Setup

Uncomment the vault volume in `docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
volumes:
  - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw
```

### UID/GID Match

The container user `hermes` has UID 1000 by default. Match it to your
host user:

```bash
docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
```

### What Works

| Operation | How |
|-----------|-----|
| Read notes | `read_file(path="/vault/note.md")` |
| Write notes | `write_file(path="/vault/note.md", content="...")` |
| Search | `search_files(pattern="...", path="/vault")` |
| Patch notes | `patch(path="/vault/note.md", old_string="...", new_string="...")` |
| Navigate | `terminal(command="ls /vault/")` |

The entrypoint detects the mount and logs whether `.obsidian/` is present.

---

## Permission Model

```bash
# Match UID to your host user
docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)
```

The container runs as user `hermes` (UID/GID 1000 by default). Rebuild with
your UID for access to vault and workspace files.

---

## Container Commands

| Command | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `docker compose up -d` | Start server in background |
| `docker compose down` | Stop server |
| `docker compose logs -f` | Follow logs |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | One-time interactive setup |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read a config value |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell |
| `docker compose run --rm hermes doctor` | Hermes diagnostics |

---

## Init Strategy -- No Stuck Wizards

The entrypoint checks on startup:

1. **config.yaml exists?** Yes -> start. No -> create minimal config.
2. **.env exists?** No -> warning with instructions.
3. **Neither exists?** Exit with error. Never stuck in a headless wizard.

---

## Autostart -- Start on Login, Stop on Logout

The project includes a **systemd --user service** that starts the container
when you log in and stops it when you log out.

### Install

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user/
cp hermes-docker.service ~/.config/systemd/user/

# Edit the path to match your project location
nano ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service
# Change WorkingDirectory to the full absolute path of your
# hermes-inside-docker directory, for example:
#   WorkingDirectory=/home/rb/hermes-inside-docker

systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable hermes-docker
systemctl --user start hermes-docker
```

### Verify

```bash
systemctl --user status hermes-docker
journalctl --user -u hermes-docker -f
```

### How It Works

- `WantedBy=default.target` -> starts when **your user session starts** (login)
- `Type=oneshot` + `RemainAfterExit=yes` -> runs `up -d`, marks as active
- systemd --user termination (logout) -> runs `ExecStop` -> `docker compose down`
- `Restart=on-failure` -> auto-restart on crash or Docker daemon restart

### Uninstall

```bash
systemctl --user stop hermes-docker
systemctl --user disable hermes-docker
rm ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service
systemctl --user daemon-reload
```

### No systemd? Desktop Autostart

If your system doesn't use systemd --user, use `.desktop` files:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/autostart/

# Start on login
cat > ~/.config/autostart/hermes-docker.desktop << 'EOF'
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=Hermes Agent
Exec=docker compose -f /home/rb/hermes-inside-docker/docker-compose.yml up -d
Terminal=false
X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true
EOF

# Stop on logout -- create a logout script in your DE settings
```

---

## Security

- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable)
- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true`
- **No capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`
- **Auth required for public bind:** Password or OAuth

## Health Check

```yaml
healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null"]
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 10s
  retries: 3
  start_period: 30s
```

TCP connect check (Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint).

## Logging

```bash
docker compose logs -f
docker compose run --rm hermes doctor
```

## Backup

```bash
tar czf hermes-config-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz hermes-config/
tar xzf hermes-config-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Container exits immediately | Config missing | Create `./hermes-config/config.yaml` |
| Cannot connect | Port not exposed | Check `docker compose ps` |
| Permission denied | UID mismatch | Rebuild with `USER_ID=$(id -u)` |
| "No API key" | `.env` missing | Add API key to `./hermes-config/.env` |
| Refuses bind 0.0.0.0 | Auth required | Add `dashboard.basic_auth` (see Auth section) |
| systemd service won't start | Wrong WorkingDirectory | Fix path in service file |

## Known Limitations

- **No desktop app build** inside container. `serve` provides JSON-RPC/WS.
- **Health check is TCP-only.** No HTTP health endpoint.
- **Large image** (~4.2 GB). Normal for Hermes -- includes ffmpeg, node,
  Python, browser agent, etc.
- **Memory:** ~200-400 MB RAM when idle.
- **`--insecure` is DEPRECATED** since June 2026 hardening. Use password auth
  or a tunnel (SSH/WireGuard).", "path": "/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker/README.md"}

{"content": "1|# =============================================================================
2|# Dockerfile – Hermes Agent (Debian Bookworm)
3|# =============================================================================
4|# Hermes Agent: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com
5|# Build: docker build -t hermes-agent:latest .
6|# =============================================================================
7|ARG DEBIAN_VERSION=bookworm
8|
9|FROM debian:${DEBIAN_VERSION}-slim AS build
10|
11|# ------------------------------------------------------------
12|# 1. System dependencies for the install script
13|# ------------------------------------------------------------
14|RUN set -eux; \
15|    apt-get update -qq; \
16|    apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
17|        ca-certificates \
18|        curl \
19|        git \
20|        libatomic1 \
21|        ; \
22|    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
23|
24|# ------------------------------------------------------------
25|# 2. Install Hermes Agent (non-interactive)
26|# ------------------------------------------------------------
27|# Installs system-wide so the hermes binary is in PATH for any user.
28|# --non-interactive skips terminal-interactive stages.
29|ARG HERMES_BRANCH=main
30|ARG HERMES_COMMIT=""
31|
32|RUN set -eux; \
33|    INSTALL_ARGS=""; \
34|    if [ -n "${HERMES_COMMIT}" ]; then \
35|      INSTALL_ARGS="${INSTALL_ARGS} --commit ${HERMES_COMMIT}"; \
36|    fi; \
37|    curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh \
38|      | bash -s -- \
39|        --non-interactive \
40|        --branch "${HERMES_BRANCH}" \
41|        --dir /opt/hermes-agent \
42|        ${INSTALL_ARGS} \
43|        ; \
44|    # The installer places the 'hermes' launcher in ~/.local/bin/
45|    export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"; \
46|    hermes_bin=$(command -v hermes); \
47|    echo "hermes binary: $hermes_bin"; \
48|    $hermes_bin --version; \
49|    # Also copy the launcher into /opt/hermes-agent for the runtime stage
50|    mkdir -p /opt/hermes-agent/bin; \
51|    cp -a "$hermes_bin" /opt/hermes-agent/bin/hermes; \
52|    # Copy .hermes tools into the repo dir so the runtime stage can find them
53|    mkdir -p /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes; \
54|    cp -a /root/.hermes /opt/hermes-agent/ 2>/dev/null || true
55|
56|# =============================================================================
57|# Runtime stage — smaller final image, no build-time dependencies
58|# =============================================================================
59|FROM debian:${DEBIAN_VERSION}-slim
60|
61|# ------------------------------------------------------------
62|# 1. Runtime system dependencies
63|# ------------------------------------------------------------
64|RUN set -eux; \
65|    apt-get update -qq; \
66|    apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
67|        ca-certificates \
68|        git \
69|        libatomic1 \
70|        ; \
71|    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
72|
73|# ------------------------------------------------------------
74|# 2. Copy Hermes from build stage
75|# ------------------------------------------------------------
76|# Copy the full Hermes installation (repo, venv, tools, and the 'hermes' launcher).
77|COPY --from=build /opt/hermes-agent /opt/hermes-agent
78|
79|# The 'hermes' launcher was copied into /opt/hermes-agent/bin/ during build.
80|# It hardcodes the hermetic tools python without the venv site-packages.
81|# We overwrite the inner launcher with a wrapper that finds the venv Python.
82|COPY hermes-launcher.sh /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes
83|RUN chmod 755 /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes && \
84|    ln -sf /opt/hermes-agent/bin/hermes /usr/local/bin/hermes
85|
86|# ------------------------------------------------------------
87|# 3. Create non-root user
88|# ------------------------------------------------------------
89|# UID/GID can be overridden at build time to match the host user.
90|ARG USER_ID=1000
91|ARG GROUP_ID=1000
92|
93|RUN set -eux; \
94|    groupadd --gid "${GROUP_ID}" --non-unique hermes; \
95|    useradd  --uid "${USER_ID}" --gid "${GROUP_ID}" \
96|             --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin \
97|             hermes; \
98|    # Make .hermes tools accessible to the non-root user, and fix any symlinks
99|    # that point to /root/.hermes/tools instead of /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/tools.
100|    find /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes -exec chmod a+r {} \; 2>/dev/null; \
101|    find /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes -type d -exec chmod a+x {} \; 2>/dev/null; \
102|    find /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes -type f \( -name "python*" -o -name "pip*" -o -name "hermes*" -o -name "activate" \) -exec chmod a+x {} \; 2>/dev/null; \
103|    find /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes -lname "/root/.hermes/tools/*" -exec sh -c 'TARGET=$(readlink "$1"); NEWTARGET=$(echo "$TARGET" | sed "s|^/root/\.hermes/|/opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/|"); ln -sf "$NEWTARGET" "$1"' _ {} \; 2>/dev/null; \
104|    chmod 755 /root; \
105|    install -d -o hermes -g hermes -m 0755 \
106|        /config \
107|        /data/rw \
108|        /vault \
109|        /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes
110|
111|# ------------------------------------------------------------
112|# 4. Volumes & environment
113|# ------------------------------------------------------------
114|# Persistent Hermes configuration (mount or named volume).
115|VOLUME /config
116|
117|# Optional Obsidian vault mount for Hermes to read/write freely.
118|VOLUME /vault
119|
120|# Read-only input data from host.
121|VOLUME /data/ro
122|
123|# Read-write working data from host.
124|VOLUME /data/rw
125|
126|ENV HERMES_HOME=/config
127|ENV HERMES_PORT=8080
128|
129|EXPOSE ${HERMES_PORT}
130|
131|# ------------------------------------------------------------
132|# 5. Entrypoint
133|# ------------------------------------------------------------
134|WORKDIR /data/rw
135|USER hermes
136|
137|COPY --chown=hermes:hermes docker-entrypoint.sh /docker-entrypoint.sh
138|RUN chmod 755 /docker-entrypoint.sh
139|
140|ENTRYPOINT ["/docker-entrypoint.sh"]

{"content": "1|#!/bin/bash
2|# =============================================================================
3|# docker-entrypoint.sh – Hermes Agent Container Entrypoint
4|# =============================================================================
5|# Responsibilities:
6|#   1. Ensure config.yaml exists (or create a minimal working one)
7|#   2. Ensure the .env secrets file exists or warn
8|#   3. Optionally detect a mounted Obsidian vault at /vault
9|#   4. Start hermes in serve mode
10|# =============================================================================
11|set -euo pipefail
12|
13|HERMES_HOME="${HERMES_HOME:-/config}"
14|HERMES_PORT="${HERMES_PORT:-8080}"
15|CONFIG_FILE="${HERMES_HOME}/config.yaml"
16|ENV_FILE="${HERMES_HOME}/.env"
17|
18|# -----------------------------------------------------------
19|# Helper: create a minimal config.yaml
20|# -----------------------------------------------------------
21|create_minimal_config() {
22|    echo "==> No Hermes configuration found. Creating minimal config.yaml ..."
23|
24|    cat > "${CONFIG_FILE}" <<- 'CONFEOF'
25|# Minimal Hermes configuration — generated by docker-entrypoint.sh
26|# Replace with your own config.yaml mounted at /config/config.yaml
27|#
28|# Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration
29|
30|# --- Model provider (required for chat, optional for serve mode) ---
31|# Set via `hermes config set` or editing this file.
32|# Uncomment and set your preferred provider:
33|#default_model: gpt-4o
34|#default_provider: openai
35|
36|# --- Server mode (serve) ---
37|# These defaults are overridden by CLI flags.
38|server:
39|  host: 0.0.0.0
40|  port: ${HERMES_PORT}
41|CONFEOF
42|
43|    sed -i "s/\${HERMES_PORT}/${HERMES_PORT}/g" "${CONFIG_FILE}"
44|    echo "==> Created ${CONFIG_FILE}"
45|}
46|
47|# -----------------------------------------------------------
48|# Helper: ensure .env exists or warn
49|# -----------------------------------------------------------
50|check_env_file() {
51|    if [ ! -f "${ENV_FILE}" ]; then
52|        cat > "${ENV_FILE}" <<- 'ENVEOF'
53|# Hermes secrets — mount your own .env to /config/.env
54|# API keys for LLM providers. At least one provider must be configured.
55|# Examples:
56|# OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
57|# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
58|# OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...
59|ENVEOF
60|        echo "==> WARNING: ${ENV_FILE} is a stub. Add your API keys before starting Hermes."
61|    fi
62|}
63|
64|# -----------------------------------------------------------
65|# Helper: detect and report an optional Obsidian vault mount
66|# -----------------------------------------------------------
67|check_vault_mount() {
68|    if [ ! -d /vault ]; then
69|        return
70|    fi
71|
72|    if [ -z "$(ls -A /vault 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
73|        echo "==> /vault is present but empty — no Obsidian vault mounted."
74|        return
75|    fi
76|
77|    if [ -d /vault/.obsidian ]; then
78|        echo "==> Obsidian vault detected at /vault (full read/write access)"
79|    else
80|        echo "==> Directory mounted at /vault (no .obsidian marker found — still usable as a writable data dir)"
81|    fi
82|}
83|
84|# -----------------------------------------------------------
85|# Main
86|# -----------------------------------------------------------
87|cd /data/rw
88|
89|case "${1:-serve}" in
90|    serve|server)
91|        if [ ! -f "${CONFIG_FILE}" ]; then
92|            create_minimal_config
93|        else
94|            echo "==> Using existing config: ${CONFIG_FILE}"
95|        fi
96|
97|        check_env_file
98|        check_vault_mount
99|
100|        if [ -d /data/rw ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u' /data/rw)" != "$(id -u)" ]; then
101|            echo "==> Adjusting /data/rw ownership to user $(id -un) ..."
102|            chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /data/rw 2>/dev/null || true
103|        fi
104|
105|        echo "==> Starting Hermes server on 0.0.0.0:${HERMES_PORT} ..."
106|        exec hermes serve \
107|            --host 0.0.0.0 \
108|            --port "${HERMES_PORT}" \
109|            --skip-build
110|        ;;
111|
112|    init|setup)
113|        echo "==> Interactive Hermes setup mode."
114|        echo "==> Configure your provider, model, and credentials."
115|        echo "==> Type 'exit' or Ctrl-D when done."
116|        echo ""
117|        exec hermes setup
118|        ;;
119|
120|    config)
121|        shift
122|        exec hermes config "$@"
123|        ;;
124|
125|    shell|bash)
126|        exec /bin/bash "$@"
127|        ;;
128|
129|    *)
130|        exec hermes "$@"
131|        ;;
